note: One primitive camping spot at an Osage River boat ramp: a gravel lot about 90 m long at the end of a gravel lane across crop fields, with a privy, and the designated spot in the strip of bank trees between the lot and the river. The river is about 20 m from the lot through that tree line. No defined pads; a rig parks on the lot. River-bottom ground that floods. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Individual Campsites'; the 1/08 map draws one Primitive Camping Area symbol beside the ramp lot and GIS has one camping point at the stored pin. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Stays under the lot rule (designated point). Privy on the map. Phone matches. Riverview kept, thin.
flags: LOT RULE (stays): the map legend has 'Primitive Camping Area' and draws one symbol immediately east of the parking lot square, beside the boat ramp and privy; GIS layer 27 has one point at 38.46345,-92.16854 (the stored pin), 33 m from the lot point. On imagery the point is in the tree strip between the gravel lot (about 90 x 15 m, running NW-SE) and the bank; there is no pad or spur at it, so a rig camps on the ramp lot itself. A designated point exists, so it is not a drop under the rule, but it is a ramp lot in practice. Owner's call if that is too thin.

WATERFRONT (stored riverview, kept): the lot's river edge is 15-25 m from the Osage (about 150 m wide here) behind a single belt of bank trees roughly 15-20 m deep; leaf-off imagery shows water through it, and the ramp cut at the lot's north end is open to the river. Not riverfront: the trees and the ramp lie between any parked rig and the water. If a tree-filtered view does not count, this goes to not waterfront - I left it because the ramp opening gives a clear view from the lot's north end.
FACILITIES: privy drawn on the map west of the lot; a small roofed structure shows there on imagery. Written as vault_toilets.
PHONE (573) 815-7900 matches the page. Pin correct. Page 170.0 acres matches.
